correctness.rationale: The complete-bipartite adjacency makes every closed-neighborhood condition a side-sum inequality and every subset-defense condition a positive-neighbor-sum threshold. The proof exhausts the possible low side sums, gives explicit feasible constructions in each upper-bound regime, and derives a contradiction from any weight-three labeling when both part sizes are at least four. The K_{2,2} boundary is independently supplied by the published cycle formula. A direct finite side-state checker confirms the formula on all part sizes two through twelve.

value.rationale: Complete bipartite graphs are a canonical exact subclass inside a problem known to remain computationally hard on bipartite graphs. The result gives a sharp structural threshold rather than a routine isolated evaluation: after the known C_4 boundary, the optimum is three exactly for smaller-part size two or three and four for all larger smaller parts. The proof identifies side-sum and positive-mass mechanisms that explain the transition.
